newsitem.title: UK: London freight market sees more activity.
newsitem.headline: London freight market sees more activity.

text.p: There was more activity generally and greater optimism from owners in the freight market on Tuesday, brokers said.
The flat October position in the U.S. Gulf appeared to be changing with better levels of fixtures and enquiries for Panamaxes and handy tonnage for grain and fertilizers.
Even the bombed-out caper market showed a shade more life with new business quoted. The BFI rose 5 points to 1034.
GRAIN --

Smart increase was seen in the U.S. Gulf/Egypt trade with reports that Seatrans conceded $12.00 for 55,000 HSS for Oct 18/24, up $2.00 from the fixture of Captain Georgis for 5,000 tonnes last week by Dreyfus.

Thalia 64,125 dwt fixed yesterday by Halla delivery U.S. Gulf end Oct trip Far East at $7,250 daily plus $125,000 was reported relet overnight to Shinwa at a premium of $150 on the daily rate and $15,000 on the bonus.

Although brokers did not see any dramatic imminent change in the U.S. Gulf market a number of Panamax orders for October shipment -- Cargill to Continent option UK, Continental to Aqaba, Toepfer to Poland, Dreyfus and Tradigrain to China, for example -- have remained unfixed.
Glencore was understood to have covered 50,000 barley from Tilbury to Saudi Arabia for prompt loading at a stronger $15.00.

Pioneer was said to have fixed an over-age Panamax from northern France to Algeria for mid-Oct at close to $6,800 daily, and there are rumours Shipmair has taken an over-age Panamax from the Plate and Brazil to the Continent.
There were reports Mosk had fixed 54,000 HSS U.S. Gulf/Japan for Nov at $20.00 basis no combo, following news that Halla booked Anaisai in this trade for end Oct/early Nov at $19.80 no combo.

Brokers expect timecharter levels for the most modern Panamaxes from U.S. Gulf to the Far East to ease up from about $10,000 daily plus $100,000 bonus to about $10,500 daily plus $140,000 bonus with the next reported fixture.
MINERALS --

In the Atlantic new caper mineral orders were quoted by Deiulemar Nouadhibou to Taranto for end Oct/early Nov, Lalemant St Lawrence to the continent, Posco, Brazil to South Korea for end Nov, and Korea Line from Brazil to China for Nov/Dec.
In the east Robe River was in the market for West Australian iron ore contracts and Bao Island for 140,000 iron ore West Australia/China for Nov 20/Dec 5.
Rumours of Richards Bay/Rotterdam coal fixtures by Cobelfret and Ankerkolen of World-Nord for end Nov and Irenes Vision for early Dec at $5.20 were discounted by brokers.

A weak fixture of 70,000 iron ore Ponta da Madeira/Adriatic by Duferco was seen for prompt loading at $7.50. But firmer Panamax fixtures were anticipated in the east where Mosk was said to be closely trading North Princess 71,200 dwt east Australia/Japan at about $8,000 daily plus $125,000 bonus.

Some brokers forecast $8,000 daily for Nopac or Australian rounds after this level was reported to have been conceded by Shinwa to Dyna Star 69,000 delivery Hong Kong for a trip via Indonesia with coal to Japan.
Amalia del Bene 64,221 dwt open prompt South Korea was understood fixed on private terms, but reports of the fixture of Atlantic Savior 64,456 dwt from Nopac were premature.
HANDY-SIZES --
Brokers reported more grain and fertilizer enquiry from the U.S. Gulf and to a lesser extent from the Continent.

Handymax turnover from the Continent to the Far East has increased with reports that Pan Ocean in particular has been busy. Grant was rumoured to have fixed 42,000 dwt and Albatross 37,000 dwt craned vessels, both at $10,300 daily in this trade.
